... SECOND INNINGS ...

For West Indies, Jason Holder gave them the opening wicket with Kemar Roach following up soon after. However, a couple of steady partnerships put them under pressure but Jayden Seales got a couple of wickets to get them back in the game. They would have expected to bowl out the Proteas a bit earlier but they let the game loose in the middle phases. However, Jomel Warrican with his four-fer, and Jayden Seales with three wickets to his name kept the pressure on the batters. The West Indies' batters will walk out in a bit aiming to start well and do a better job than what they did in England.

Jayden Seales seals things off for the first innings and South Africa ends up with 357 on the board. They were dealt an early blow with the wicket of Aiden Markram but Tony de Zorzi and Tristan Stubbs managed to stabilize the innings. Temba Bavuma played a captain's knock later and made sure to stay put at one end while they lost some wickets at the other. A couple of stable partnerships in the middle order got them to a good score but the lower order could not contribute much to that. Only 13 runs were added to the score since the start of play today which is not what the Proteas would have expected. Tony de Zorzi with 78 runs to his name and Temba Bavuma scoring 86 would be the highlight of the batting unit. They will now aim to do well with the ball and get themselves a considerable lead.

PITCH REPORT - Nikhil Uttamchandani is pitchside along with Darren Ganga. He starts by addressing the sun which is shining in all its glory. Hopes that we get a good game of cricket. Informs that the spinners will have plenty of purchase on offer from this used deck. States that the deck is slowing down, and the batters must take this factor into consideration.

Wiaan Mulder is in for a chat. He reckons that the surface might deteriorate a little bit. Adds that there are a few scuff marks but the pitch played pretty well. Tells that it was difficult to score due to the defensive fields set by West Indies. Hopes that the pitch starts to turn at some stage. Further says that they will try to put as many as they can and if they bowl well, it will put them in a good position.

The weather has certainly kept us on our toes here in Trinidad. Day 1 was frustrating, with just 15 overs possible, but thankfully, the rain stayed away for most of Day 2, barring a brief delay at the start of the post-Lunch session. As we head into Day 3, fingers are crossed that the rain gods continue to show mercy, allowing us to witness a full day's play and some riveting Test cricket!

The West Indies, buoyed by a late surge last evening, will be eager to wrap up the innings quickly and then put the South African bowlers under pressure. With the pitch showing signs of wear and tear, it could be crucial in determining the course of this match.

Hello and a warm welcome to Day 3 of this enthralling Test match between South Africa and the West Indies! After a rain-marred opening day and a fiercely competitive Day 2, we're all set for another absorbing day of cricket. South Africa, at 344/8, have laid a solid foundation thanks to a string of valuable partnerships. Wiaan Mulder, unbeaten on 37, will look to push his team closer to the 400 mark, with Kagiso Rabada for company.
... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

Right then, that's it from an entertaining day of cricket, with both sides locked in an evenly-balanced contest. The action is set to continue on Day 3, starting at 7 pm IST (1.30 pm GMT). Be sure to tune in early for all the pre-game build-up. Until then, cheers and goodbye!

Jomel Warrican is up for a chat. He says that the pitch was flat and he tried to keep things tight and it was a great effort to take 7 wickets in the day. Adds that he coordinated with his partner Gudakesh Motie to try out different strategies in the inning. Concludes by saying that they would try to wrap up things as soon as possible on Day 3 and then bat well to try and take the lead.

South Africa had a productive first session leading up to Lunch, scoring 107 runs in 38 overs while losing two wickets, including the important late dismissal of Tony de Zorzi. The session started under clear skies, allowing the Proteas to build momentum. Tony de Zorzi played fluently, notching up his second Test half-century and forming a solid 50-run partnership with Temba Bavuma. West Indies gradually clawed their way back into the game with tight bowling that did stem the flow of runs. Jomel Warrican managed to dismiss the well-set de Zorzi giving a big sigh of relief to the home side heading to Lunch.

In the afternoon session, following a brief delay caused by a passing shower during the break, the Proteas duo of Temba Bavuma and David Bedingham resumed play with a strong start. Just as Bedingham began to accelerate the scoring, Jayden Seales struck, sending him back with the help of a brilliant diving catch by debutant Keacy Carty. Ryan Rickelton then joined Bavuma at the crease, forming a solid partnership that guided South Africa through the remainder of the session without further setbacks racking 92 runs off the 27 overs.

Jayden Seales once again proved to be a crucial asset for captain Kraigg Brathwaite, returning to the attack to claim the prized wicket of Temba Bavuma, who was looking dangerous with his 86-run knock. However, despite this key breakthrough, West Indies couldn’t fully capitalize, allowing the incoming batter to settle in. Both Wiaan Mulder and Kyle Verreynne took advantage of the weary West Indies bowlers, significantly upping the scoring rate in the last half-hour of the day. But just when South Africa seemed to be gaining control, Jomel Warrican turned the tide, striking twice in two balls to give West Indies the strong finish they were looking for. Despite losing wickets at regular intervals, South Africa's four 50-run partnerships in the middle have put them in a strong position heading into Day 3 on which they will look to push home the advantage.

West Indies initially seized control of the session right after Tea, with Kemar Roach striking in the very first over to dismiss Ryan Rickelton. The Proteas found themselves under pressure as the West Indian pacers delivered a series of probing overs. However, with Temba Bavuma well-set at one end, South Africa managed to keep things steady. Kyle Verreynne offered solid support, holding his ground with firm defence and keeping the scoreboard ticking alongside his skipper.

SESSION SUMMARY - 33 Overs, 100 Runs, 4 Wickets. After the disappointment of Day 1 being washed out with only 15 overs possible, Day 2 lived up to expectations, offering uninterrupted action throughout. The day was evenly contested, leaving both sides with mixed feelings. South Africa find themselves at 344/8, with Wiaan Mulder solid on 37, supported by Kagiso Rabada at the other end. West Indies will be buoyed by those two late wickets, providing them with much-needed momentum heading into Day 3 after a day of hard-fought cricket.

SESSION SUMMARY - 27 overs, 92 runs and 1 wicket. Apart from that short delay at the start, we once again were treated with some good uninterrupted game of cricket. South Africa were quite senational at the fag end of this session, they kept scoring runs freely and are looking solid at 244/4 at the end of 80 overs and the players head off for a Tea break. An intriguing session nonetheless, with both teams having a crack at each other. West Indies got rid of David Bedingham just when he started to accelerate the innings, but since then they had no joy coming their way. Temba Bavuma and Ryan Rickelton have forged a solid stand here and head into the break with the momentum on their side. Temba Bavuma leads from the front here, and will be eyeing to covert his half-century into a big score when he comes out to bat. West Indies will be aiming to break this stand as soon as possible, and make a sharp comeback later on. We will back for the final session on Day 2 at 12.30 am IST (7 pm GMT, previous day). Do join us to find out how things pan out.

UPDATE - 10.10 pm IST (4.40 pm GMT) - Great news! The drizzle has eased, and the skies have brightened over Queen's Park Oval, indicating that the delay for the second session won't be too long. However there is a big dark cloud hovering around but the covers are being removed, which is a promising sign. Stay tuned for more updates as the action looks set to resume shortly!
... DAY 2, SESSION 2 ...

West Indies came into the morning session, with the momentum on their side, but with no dark clouds hovering around, they were always going to find it difficult to dictate terms with the ball and that is what happened. Kemar Roach was slightly making it easier for the batters, as he kept attacking the batters with full-length deliveries, which kept backfiring. He though eventually got the better of Tristan Stubbs which might've given him some confidence. Gudakesh Motie was way better as compared to yesterday, he kept it pretty tight during his spell, which helped his team tremendously. West Indies will surely be happier after seeing the back of Tony de Zorzi and would be hoping to capitalize on the momentum after the break. The restart is supposed to happen at 10.10 pm IST (4.40 pm GMT), but as mentioned before, RAIN HAS ARRIVED once again at Port of Spain. Let us keep our fingers crossed and hope it is just a passing shower and we get to see another uninterrupted session. Stay tuned for more updates...

Tony de Zorzi grew into the innings really well, and his positive start allowed him to rack up his second half-century in Tests. He kept his approach pretty simple even when he was joined by Temba Bavuma in the middle. This pair stitched a solid 50-run stand, and were in a great position to see off this session. Although Jomel Warrican had other ideas. The West Indies decided to work with two spinners in tandem at the fag end of this session, which did wonders for the hosts, as Tony de Zorzi who took Gudakesh Motie to the cleaners on Day 1, got excited after seeing spin from both ends, but it did not pan out the way he wanted it too.

South Africa were cautious at the start of Day 1, but with the sun shining in all its glory, the Proteas came out with the right intent and instantly put the bowling side under some pressure. Tony de Zorzi and Tristan Stubbs were quite solid in the middle. Their approach was outstanding with both the batters picking up the bad balls really well and putting them away, which kept the scoreboard ticking. They were consistently keeping the scoring rate near the 3-run mark. It was all going hunky dory for them, with these two stitching a 43-run stand for the second wicket, but Tristan Stubbs could not stick around for long and their vision to remain unscathed was washed away.

Just at the brink of Lunch, we could see some droplets coming down, but just in a form of mizzle, which isn't haunting after all the chaos we witnessed yesterday. Fortunately though, we had an uninterrupted session here, which was an intriguing one as well. This session saw 107 runs being scored in 38 overs, with the hosts picking up two wickets, one was the late dismissal of the set-batter which takes them into this Lunch break with an upper hand.

Commentary.Commentary: Under the clear blue skies of Port of Spain, all is set for the action-packed Day 2 to begin! The umpires lead the way onto the field, followed by the West Indies players who quickly take their positions, eager to build on yesterday's momentum. Tony de Zorzi and Tristan Stubbs stride out to the crease, ready to continue their innings for South Africa. With the ball in hand, Jason Holder is poised to kick off the day's proceedings for West Indies! Away we go!

PITCH REPORT - Samuel Badree is alongside Stacy Ann King in the middle. Badree says the sunshine is out and despite a lot of rain yesterday the drainage here has been tremendous to get the outfield ready for a timely start. Stacy Ann King says the groundstaff did very well to keep the deck covered and the deck looks dry suggesting that the odd balls could keep low. Further adds that the bowlers will have to work around and keep it tight around the off-stump mark.

West Indies' pacers will aim to keep their lines and lengths tight, hoping for a couple of quick wickets as a bonus. Left-arm spinner Gudakesh Motie had a tough Day 1 with little turn on offer, but some advice from coach Andre Coley could turn things around. The weather looks mostly sunny, though there's a slight chance of a shower. Fingers crossed for uninterrupted cricket! The big question: Can the Proteas stay composed and show intent, or will the Windies carry their momentum into Day 2? Let’s find out.

South Africa started cautiously on Day 1, with openers Tony de Zorzi and Aiden Markram showing promise. While Zorzi settled in for a big score, Markram couldn't hold his ground. Now, Tristan Stubbs will join Zorzi to kick off Day 2, aiming to keep the scoreboard moving. The last time the Proteas faced the Windies here in 2010, they came out on top, but the Windies have been tough to beat at this venue since.

Welcome, cricket fans, to Day 2 of the first Test between South Africa and West Indies! Day 1 was a washout, with rain allowing just 15 overs. The Proteas managed 45 runs but lost a wicket just before play was halted. But good news—chances of rain are low today, so get ready for an action-packed day ahead!
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

Well, on DAY 1 of this Test match it is the rain gods who come out on top, as the PLAY HAS BEEN ABANDONED ON DAY 1. It was a very short affair to be honest, we just saw 15 overs being played after South Africa elected to bat first. They got off to a cautious start, with Kemar Roach and Jayden Seales dictating the terms with the new ball. It was Jason Holder who fold the only wicket of this match so far, with Tristan Stubbs coming out to face just 5 deliveries before the rain interrupted play. The weather forecast for the day, was quite promising, but against all odds, the rain gods were the one's who had a ball. Unfortunately, that's it from DAY 1. The action will continue on 8th August, 2024, and due to a lot of overs being lost, we will have an early start on DAY 2. Play will start at 7 pm IST (1.30 pm GMT). But you can join us early for the build-up. ADIOS!

As we wait, let’s take a quick look around the world of Olympics. Four-time Olympic medalist Timo Boll has retired from his illustrious 30-year table tennis career after being knocked out in the quarter-final match. India's Vinesh Phogat faced a heartbreaking disqualification in the finals of the 50-kg wrestling category for being overweight by 100 grams. Meanwhile, 51-year-old British skateboarder Andy Macdonald wrapped up his Paris Olympics with a stellar run, delighting skateboarding fans worldwide as he finished with a score of 77.66, securing 18th place in the heat.

For West Indies, Kemar Roach's return and disciplined bowling have been significant positives. Jayden Seales has also maintained tight lines, but spinner Gudakesh Motie has yet to find any assistance from the pitch. Jason Holder striking with his first ball will give West Indies hope that the pitch is still conducive for bowlers, provided they maintain tight lines, something they have marginally failed to do so far. With rain still persistent, the early lunch break might extend a bit longer. However, we remain hopeful that the overhead conditions will improve as the groundsmen work diligently to dry the soaked patches on the outfield. Stay tuned for further updates.

The visitors won the toss and elected to bat first on a pitch that looked perfect for batting. West Indies pacers, Kemar Roach and Jayden Seales, bowled tightly but didn't raise any major concerns for the opening pair. Tony de Zorzi set himself up very nicely in the middle with a cautious start, which he then transitioned into an aggressive approach against the spinner, Gudakesh Motie. Aiden Markram, on the other hand, never looked fully settled at the crease, and after facing 34 balls, he missed one from Jason Holder that struck the stumps, leading to his dismissal.

SESSION SUMMARY - 15 Overs, 45 Runs, 1 Wicket. West Indies will not be very happy about how the first session of Day 1 concluded with rain interrupting their momentum. They started strong with the ball and just when they got themselves the first breakthrough, the rain gods decided to arrive. South Africa will certainly be disappointed with the loss of Aiden Markram after a cautious start ending at 45/1.

Commentary.Commentary: With all the pre-match formalities complete, it’s time for the action to begin! The two umpires stride to the centre, followed by West Indies players who spread out to take their positions. Aiden Markram and Tony de Zorzi are ready as the opening batters for South Africa, making their way to the crease to start the innings. Kemar Roach is handed the new ball and is on top of his mark raring to go. Let's play says the umpire and here we go..
The players now line up on either side of the trophy in preparation for the national anthems. First, the South African anthem will be played, followed by the national anthem of the West Indies.

PITCH REPORT - Vernon Philander is down by the pitch and says the deck looks like a belter of a wicket for batters. Adds that there is no grass on the pitch and might slow up for the seamers who could initially get some seam and bounce considering the overhead conditions and the dukes ball but teams should make the most of this surface by batting first.

Kraigg Brathwaite, the skipper of West Indies says they would have wanted to bat first as well. Adds that he expects improvement from the last time and hopes to have positive results. He further says that discipline is the main point that they need to focus on. Concludes by saying that they have one debutant Keacy Carty who will be batting at number three.

Temba Bavuma, the captain of South Africa announces that they will bat first, believing the batting conditions are favourable. He sees it as a good opportunity for their batters to settle in well and expects a challenging test for their inexperienced side. Bavuma mentions that there are no debutants, just a different mix in their setup.

South Africa (Playing XI) - Tony de Zorzi, Aiden Markram, Tristan Stubbs, Temba Bavuma (C), David Bedingham, Ryan Rickelton, Kyle Verreynne (WK), Wiaan Mulder, Keshav Maharaj, Kagiso Rabada, Lungi Ngidi.

West Indies (Playing XI) - Kraigg Brathwaite (C), Mikyle Louis, Alick Athanaze, Keacy Carty, Kavem Hodge, Jason Holder, Joshua Da Silva (WK), Gudakesh Motie, Kemar Roach, Jayden Seales, Jomel Warrican.
TOSS - The coin flip lands in the favour of South Africa and they opt to BAT first.

It's only fair to say that both teams are evenly matched, making this an exhilarating contest with the potential to shift the dynamics of the trophy, which has mostly been a one-sided affair. Both sides will also be eager to improve their standings on the WTC table. Will this rejuvenated South African squad maintain their dominance over West Indies, or will the hosts make history? The answer is just moments away, as the toss is imminent.

On the other hand, South Africa is in the midst of rebuilding their red-ball team. Although they lack extensive Test experience, they have players who have demonstrated their temperament and will be poised to seize this opportunity and make a significant impact away from home. With a relatively new batting lineup, much of the team’s fortunes will depend on Tony de Zorzi to deliver a strong start at the top of the order alongside Aiden Markram. Tristan Stubbs will be crucial in addressing the long-standing concern over the number three spot for the Proteas. The team has opted to include an additional batter, Ryan Rickelton, while much attention will also be focused on David Bedingham, who is expected to play a pivotal role in this lineup.

Despite three consecutive test losses before this match, West Indies have plenty of positives to build on and will be very confident of a strong performance at home. The return of Kemar Roach is a significant boost, as he could be a real force alongside Jayden Seales. With Kavem Hodge in excellent recent form, much will depend on him to anchor the batting in the middle order. The team has chosen to go with two spinners, Gudakesh Motie and Jomel Warrican, leaving Shamar Joseph out of the XI. This game also marks a special occasion for Keacy Carty, who makes his debut and will be looking to make a strong impact.

Hello and a warm welcome to the 1st Test match of this year's Sir Vivian Richards Trophy, coming to you from Queen's Park Oval in Trinidad. The West Indies host South Africa in a two-match red ball battle, which will be followed by a three-match T20I series. Historically, South Africa have dominated, never losing a Test series to West Indies and maintaining a formidable record. However, this South African squad may lack the experience and intensity of any past teams, giving the West Indies a significant chance to break the streak and claim the trophy for the first time.
